Subject: SLA appendix — initial questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is the SLA appendix referenced in section 4. Our procurement and legal teams have a few clarifying questions about how Redwood measures uptime/latency and how service credits would be applied. Could you please provide: 

- A concise definition of "availability" for hosted API endpoints (what counts as up vs down).
- How latency SLOs are measured (p50/p95/p99; windowing; what endpoints and payload sizes used).
- The measurement tooling and whether Acme can run an independent probe.
- A service credit table with thresholds and credit percentages (monthly measurement).
- Exclusions (maintenances, force majeure, customer-induced outages).

We attached the specific questionnaire file (Acme_RFP_SLA_Appendix.pdf). Please let us know if you'd prefer to answer inline or provide a short annex we can include in the contract. We have a tentative procurement deadline of 2026-04-25.

Subject: Re: SLA appendix — initial questions (SLO table & measurement methodology)

Hi all — please see inline responses and an agreed SLO table below. I kept language concise for contract annex use; we can expand definitions in an attached "SLO definitions" CSV.

1) Availability (uptime) definition:
- "Availability" = percentage of 5xx or connection-failure-free successful API interactions for Redwood-hosted inference endpoints, measured as the fraction of successful request completions returning HTTP 200/202/204 where application-level errors (4xx) are considered successful delivery unless they indicate platform failure. Exclusions: customer misconfiguration, customer-originated network failures, scheduled maintenance windows (see below), and force majeure.

2) Latency measurement:
- Targeted endpoints: /v1/generate (text), /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings.
- Metric: end-to-end server response latency measured at Redwood ingress (time between request reception and final token emission completion).
- SLOs (monthly rolling window, UTC):
  * Availability (monthly): 99.95% uptime
  * Latency (text-generation, typical 1-2k token requests): p95 <= 1.2s, p99 <= 3.0s
  * Embeddings (small payloads): p95 <= 250ms
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day window, calculated daily. Percentiles computed on successful requests only.

3) Measurement tooling and probes:
- Primary measurement: Redwood's telemetry pipeline (internal collector + Prometheus-derived SLO service) using production traffic and synthetic canaries.
- Independent monitoring: Acme may run external probes. For credits, we will reconcile using Redwood's production telemetry; if Acme provides independent measurement, both sides will compare windowed summaries and engage joint validation before issuing credits.

4) Service credit schedule (monthly window):
- Availability >= 99.95%: 0% credit
- Availability >= 99.90% and < 99.95%: 5% monthly service credit
- Availability >= 99.0% and < 99.90%: 15% monthly service credit
- Availability < 99.0%: 30% monthly service credit
- Credits cap: maximum 100% of monthly service fee for the impacted subscription period.

5) Measurement & reporting process:
- Redwood will publish a monthly SLO report (rolling 30-day numbers) and incident impact summaries. Credits are applied after validation; Acme has 30 days from report availability to dispute with supporting telemetry.

6) Scheduled maintenance & emergency maintenance:
- Scheduled maintenance: Redwood will provide at least 72 hours' notice for non-critical maintenance windows; these will be excluded from uptime calculations if they are announced.
- Emergency maintenance: events required to remediate critical stability/security issues may be excluded if they meet the emergency maintenance criteria; Redwood will provide post-event disclosure.

7) Additional notes:
- For Dedicated/Private deployments we will provide separate measurement endpoints and can accommodate tighter rolling windows upon request; any deviation will be called out in the contract exhibit.

I've attached the SLO definitions CSV for insertion into the annex (slo_definitions.csv). If this looks good I recommend we convert it into a contract exhibit with the exclusions and dispute resolution paragraphs (legal to redline).

Regards,

Marissa — thanks for the speedy and detailed response. A few clarifying questions from Procurement/Legal: 

- Can you confirm that scheduled maintenance windows will be limited to X hours/month and that we will be notified via both email and the status page?
- For independent probes: if Acme's external probe shows a discrepancy vs Redwood's telemetry, what's the escalation path and typical time-to-validate?
- Are customer-induced outages (e.g., malformed payloads that cause repeated retries) always excluded from uptime? We may want stricter language around "customer-originated network failures" to avoid disputes.

Also, we need a DocuSign-ready annex. Could you provide a one-page exhibit we can push through signature?

Thanks — aiming to close commercial terms week of 4/20.

Jill

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Summers <jill.summers@acme-corp.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA appendix — initial questions (SLO table & measurement methodology)

Jill/Tom — thanks for the follow-ups, and glad the draft is useful. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Scheduled maintenance: we commit to a target of <= 6 hours/month for non-critical maintenance for hosted customers. Notices will be sent by email and posted to status.redwood.ai at least 72 hours in advance. We'll include the 6-hour target in the exhibit (with a short "good-faith" language that occasional bursts due to rolling upgrades could temporarily exceed this target with notice).
- Independent probe discrepancies: standard process — Acme opens a support ticket with summary window + probe logs; Redwood engineering will acknowledge within 4 business hours, provide a preliminary reconciliation within 48 hours, and a final validation within 10 business days. If discrepancy remains, a joint telemetry review will occur; we will not apply credits until both sides agree on scope and impact. We'll include the timelines in the annex.
- Customer-induced outages: we will enumerate exclusions, including persistent malformed payloads that lead to customer-side throttles or connection resets. We can tighten the language around "customer-originated network failures" to list examples (carrier outages, VPC routing, customer auth misconfiguration).

Next steps: Marissa will convert the SLO table into an annex (one-page, DocuSign-ready) and we'll post it to the shared drive. I've provisionally placed the draft and links here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Acme-SLA-Draft and created a DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.net/DocuSignEnvelope/Acme-RW-0042.

If Acme is comfortable, we're prepared to include the above SLOs and the service credit schedule as the commercial exhibit and proceed to signature. We're also willing to include a one-time goodwill migration credit (10% of first-month fee) if there's a measurable migration delay caused by Redwood.

Thanks — will await final confirmation from Legal and Procurement.

Best,
Neha
Head of GTM Operations, Redwood Inference
